solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Creeps give advice to heartless employers

parts.note: to tip is to give someone advice, as a racing tipster does
taken as written

indicators.note: with its heart removed, the word employers keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A complaint that bosses with no heart need some counsel.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to walk stealthily on the balls of the feet, which is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Revealing how Mandy appears to change sex

definitions.meaning: describing a garment or outfit that exposes the breasts

definitions.text: how Mandy appears to change sex
definitions.meaning: the girl's name with its top letter lost becomes Andy, a boy's name

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads 'top-less': take the top (first) letter off MANDY and you have ANDY, so she seems to have turned into a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A topless outfit exposes the upper body, so it is revealing in the clothing sense.

clue.text: Irishman, mostly cunning, like Abraham was

indicators.note: mostly means the name loses its final letters, keeping most of it

parts.note: Patrick is the archetypal Irish man's name, after the patron saint
arch means sly or knowing

explanation.surface: Describing a crafty Irishman as resembling a biblical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham is the first of the Old Testament founding fathers of Israel, so he was a revered tribal elder.

clue.text: Colour regularly found among coach-horses

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the hyphenated phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A shade often seen on horses that pull coaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment and shade, a specific colour.

clue.text: Understaffed, editor's off — secretary can take it!

indicators.note: off means the editor's abbreviation is removed from the longer word

parts.note: short-handed means lacking enough workers
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An office short of staff with the editor away, but the secretary can cope.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the playful closing phrase: what a secretary takes down at dictation.
explanation.definitionFit: Secretaries traditionally took dictation in a system of quick abbreviated symbols, so it is what they take.

clue.text: There can be one of three

definitions.text: There can be one of three

parts.words: There can be one of three
parts.note: the word 'There' is a rearrangement of the letters of 'three'

explanation.surface: A remark that one item could come from a set of three.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'There' as a word: its letters rearranged give 'three', so 'There' is a jumble of 'three'.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging another word's letters is what the term names.

clue.text: Suit a particular colour? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the colour word falls one letter short at its end

parts.note: green is one specific colour

explanation.surface: Asking whether a certain shade would suit someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To suit is to agree, as when a climate agrees with someone or a plan agrees with them.

clue.text: "Correction" — last word many people have time for

parts.note: amen is the final word of a prayer
D is 500 in Roman numerals, a crossword stand-in for many
men means people

explanation.surface: A request that a final word be corrected, with many people having time for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change made to correct or improve a text, a synonym.

clue.text: Show to see twice, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the clue's phrase is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to review is to look at something again

explanation.surface: A show worth seeing twice, according to report.
explanation.walkthrough: A REVUE is a variety show of sketches and songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a theatrical entertainment of short sketches and songs, a type of show.

clue.text: Badly treats a young girl without work

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the girl wraps round the work

parts.note: Miss is a title for a young girl
use means to work or operate

explanation.surface: Accusing someone of mistreating an unemployed young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To misuse someone is to treat them wrongly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Many games require it to toss

definitions.meaning: a playing field for sports such as cricket or football
to ... something is to throw it

explanation.definitionFit: A pitch is a sports field and also a verb meaning to throw, giving two senses.

clue.text: What belongs to us little people, Ukip's prime concern?

parts.note: ours is what belongs to us
elves are the little people of folklore

explanation.surface: A wry joke about a British nationalist party caring mainly about its own people.
explanation.walkthrough: Ukip is the UK Independence Party, a British party campaigning for independence from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A party focused on national self-interest is primarily concerned with its own people, us.

clue.text: The most shocking of locations, perhaps

definitions.text: The most shocking of locations, perhaps

parts.words: The most shocking of locations, perhaps
parts.note: shocking refers to an earthquake's shocks, strongest at their point of origin

explanation.surface: A claim about the most scandalous place.
explanation.definitionFit: The point on the surface directly above an earthquake's focus, where the shaking is greatest.

clue.text: Freak tides causing stones to vanish

indicators.note: freak describes the word tides as abnormal, so its letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Unusual tides making pebbles disappear from a beach.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight (14 pounds), so 'stones vanishing' is weight loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Slimming regimes are meant to make pounds and stones of body weight disappear.

clue.text: Cancel clean-up

definitions.meaning: to ... a plan is to call it off

explanation.definitionFit: Scrub means both to call off and a thorough wash, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: She performs on 1 across

parts.note: the answer to 1 across, read as the tips of the feet, describes how this performer dances

explanation.surface: A woman who performs on the first answer in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A classical dancer who performs en pointe, on the tips of the feet.

clue.text: Talks to commercial outfits

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
dresses are outfits

explanation.surface: Speaking to businesses that sell clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To address someone is to speak to them directly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: The vicar's time to relax? Hardly!

definitions.text: The vicar's time to relax? Hardly!

parts.words: The vicar's time to relax? Hardly!
parts.note: Sunday is meant to be a rest day, yet it is the busiest day for a parish priest

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a clergyman gets any time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunday is the sabbath, set aside for rest, but clergy work hardest then.

clue.text: Sounds like Cook lied about where the silver came from

indicators.note: sounds like means the cook word is heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a chef is a cook

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of lied are moved around

explanation.surface: A scandal about a cook lying over the origin of the silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire city of Sheffield is famed for cutlery and Sheffield plate, a silver-plated ware.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheffield is the English city famous for its silverware and plated cutlery.

clue.text: Not working, I only had love, unfortunately

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the words have been jumbled into a sorry state

explanation.surface: Someone lamenting that a break off work held nothing but romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on vacation is away from work, so not working.

clue.text: Start with a song in such a theatre

parts.note: to open is to start
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: Advice to begin a show in an outdoor venue with a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces; 'in such a theatre' describes an outdoor venue.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air theatre is one staged outdoors without a roof.

clue.text: Soldiers compose letter from abroad

definitions.meaning: ..., the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers
a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'The TA', the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve; 'compose' is a link meaning 'make up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet, so a foreign letter.

clue.text: Provides help as Jenny sits spinning

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey, an ass

indicators.note: spinning means the letters of sits are turned around and mixed

explanation.surface: A helper while Jenny sits at a spinning wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jenny' looks like a woman's name, and a spinning jenny was a machine, but here a jenny is a she-donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help, so it provides help.

clue.text: Spooky l-lake

indicators.note: the stammered first letter means the lake's name starts with its first letter said twice

parts.note: Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes
Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A stammered word about a creepy lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer in 'l-lake' tells you to stutter the lake's name: E-ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and frightening, a synonym of spooky.

clue.text: Badger some councillor at elections

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pestering a council member at polling time.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel or honey badger is an African badger species, an example of the animal.

clue.text: Some convicts hiding behind emergency gear at sea

indicators.note: hiding means the convicts conceal the other word within them

parts.note: lifers are convicts serving life sentences, one kind of prisoner
aft means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Escaped prisoners hiding behind safety kit on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflatable boats carried for abandoning ship are emergency equipment at sea.

clue.text: One of those bloodsuckers locked up by policemen

definitions.text: One of those bloodsuckers locked up by policemen

parts.words: One of those bloodsuckers locked up by policemen
parts.note: the word policemen contains a run of letters naming parasites, and the answer is one of them

explanation.surface: A leech-like crook arrested by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'po-LICE-men' sit LICE; the answer is one of these, the singular.
explanation.definitionFit: Lice are small blood-sucking parasitic insects; the singular is one of them.

clue.text: Endless noise upsets the horse catcher

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsets means the letters are turned upside down, read backwards
endless means the noise word loses its last letter

parts.note: a report is a loud bang

explanation.surface: A loud noise startles the horse catcher.
explanation.walkthrough: REPORT less its end is REPOR; 'upsets' turns it upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A roper is one who lassoes animals such as horses, so a horse catcher.

clue.text: Quality attire but looking out of place

indicators.note: looking out of place means the letters are displaced into a new order

explanation.surface: Clothing that looks wrong despite being good.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a characteristic or quality, a synonym.

clue.text: How to work ejector seat? It's meant to be printed

definitions.meaning: push the button that frees the pilot
an official statement issued to newspapers for publication

explanation.walkthrough: Read the first definition as two instructions: push, then let go.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement issued to the media for publication, and literally pushing a release button.

clue.text: See 26
Businesses employ one to make angry speeches

indicators.note: employ means the businesses take in the numeral as a worker

parts.note: trades are businesses or occupations
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Firms hiring someone to deliver furious rants.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry outburst of speech, so the plural is a match.
